question: Ultrasound is preferred over CT for detecting and characterising pleural effusion in a child with paediatric chest infection, because it avoids ionising radiation and can guide drainage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Ultrasound IS the preferred second-line modality for pleural fluid in children. It is radiation-free, available at the bedside, and guides drainage procedures. CT adds dose and rarely changes initial management of an effusion.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Ultrasound detects effusion reliably, characterises it as free or loculated, and can guide pleural drainage — all without ionising radiation. CT is reserved for parenchymal complications not clarified by CXR + ultrasound.
